messages:
oliver: Escalating — customer (sarah) sees requests from eu-west1 routed to us-east-1 repeatedly. High p50/p95 latency + some 401s for short bursts.
sarah-cust: Seeing ~150-300ms extra per request and intermittent 401s. We scoped API keys per-region; when routed to us-east the token fails.
oliver: Repro steps from customer: curl with
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <eu-key>" -H "X-Forwarded-For: 35.180.12.4" -H "X-Region-Hint: eu-west1" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
Headers show X-Region-Hint set. But logs show gateway forwarded to us-east pool.
maya: Can you grab the gateway proxy/access logs (envoy) for one of the failed requests? Also any gateway hostrewrite or route config for that customer service?
oliver: Pasted snippet from customer log (timestamped):
  PROXY-IN: path=/v1/generate, host=api.redwood.example.com, x-region-hint=eu-west1, auth=OK
  ROUTER-OUT: cluster=us-east-gw, x-detected-region=us-east1, upstream=10.2.3.4:8443
Looks like header present but routing chooses us-east cluster.
ricardo: Possible that L7 route match is doing header-based matching before a host_rewrite or route action that mutates host, causing route table to fall through to default. Is the customer using any custom domain / host rewrite? Any TLS SNI differences?
oliver: Customer uses our standard api domain, no custom host. They said this started after the last gateway config change last week.
maya: Deploy-bot output shows rollout at 2026-02-27 03:14 UTC for envoy-route-config v2.1.8 -> v2.2.0 with a small change: added host_rewrite for internal routing to regional pools. Could be related.
ricardo: Hypothesis: host_rewrite combined with L7 header routing causes header to be lost/normalized and header-based routing rule to not match, falling back to default cluster (us-east). I'll try to reproduce locally with same config.
oliver: Customer provided a sample request id: req-0a9f3b2c. Logs attached by support (linked) — they show 401s only when routed to us-east. When routed to eu-west requests succeed.
maya: Quick mitigation — add an emergency route rule in gateway to honor X-Region-Hint as a top-level explicit match before host_rewrite. That should keep eu traffic sticky. I can roll a canary patch to a few proxies.
ricardo: Repro steps I'm running:
  - start envoy with our route config v2.2.0 locally
  - send requests with X-Region-Hint: eu-west1
  - observe route decision and check headers pre/post host_rewrite
If I can reproduce, I'll prepare a minimal failing config and submit PR to revert the host_rewrite ordering.
oliver: Customer asked about billing impact — tickets show duplicated ingress rounding but main issue is latency/auth failures. I'll update them that we're investigating and offering to temporarily route them to dedicated eu pool while we patch.
sarah-cust: Appreciate quick response. Temporary workaround is fine. Let us know ETA.
maya: Starting canary: pin rule to match x-region-hint as PRIORITY 1000 on 3 proxies in eu region. Rolling now. I'll monitor for anomaly.
deploy-bot: canary deployment started: route-fix-eu-hint -> proxies: eu-proxy-1, eu-proxy-2, eu-proxy-3. Rollout id: r-20260228-11
ricardo: I reproduced locally. Bug: envoy normalizer removes custom x-* header during host_rewrite stage if header match is in a later phase. Patch ready to reorder matcher evaluation to preserve header checks before host mutation. Will open PR.
maya: Can we keep the emergency canary and then merge the PR to main after CI? If tests pass we promote.
oliver: I'll keep customer updated and offer a credit for the 2 hours of degraded traffic.
sarah-cust: Thanks — will verify next 30 mins and confirm.
ricardo: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/envoy-config/pull/542 — fixes matcher order, adds unit test for header-preserve scenario.
maya: Monitoring looks better on canary after 5m: latency back to normal and no 401s. I'll extend to 12 proxies and then full rollout if stable. :thumbsup:
oliver: Closing loop once full rollout done. Thanks everyone.
